children: Basis bids for corn shipped by barge to the U.S. Gulf Coast declined on Tuesday, reflecting pressure from early harvest activity in southern areas, while soybean barge bids were mixed, traders said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture said the corn harvest was 5% complete nationally as of Sunday, ahead of the five-year average of 3%. By state, harvest progress reached 30% in Tennessee, 19% in Kentucky and 14% in Missouri, each ahead of the respective state averages for this time of year.
Some brokers were encouraging farmers to sell grain as Chicago Board of Trade corn futures
hovered near three-year highs set last week.

Meanwhile, as harvesting ramps up, rising freight costs helped support CIF values at the Gulf. Harvest activity has boosted demand for barges at a time when Midwest river levels are declining, prompting shippers to load less cargo per barge, a freight source said.
At the Gulf, CIF corn barges loaded in September were offered at 75 cents over CBOT December (CZ26) futures.
October corn barges traded at 86 cents over futures and were re-bid at 85 cents over futures, down 3 cents from Friday's bid.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in the first half of October were steady at around 105 cents over CBOT December futures.
For soybeans, CIF soy barges loaded in September were bid at 97 cents over CBOT November (SX26) futures, down 7 cents from Friday, while October barges were bid at 110 cents over futures, up 2 cents.
Soybean barges loaded in December traded at 108 and 110 cents over CBOT January (SF27) futures.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybean shipments in October held steady at around 127 cents over CBOT November futures.
The USDA reported export inspections of U.S. corn in the latest week at 1,662,496 metric tons, topping a range of trade expectations for 1,200,000 to 1,550,000 tons.
Soybean export inspections totaled 422,016 tons, in line with expectations for 350,000 to 600,000 tons.
